title: perf-canary: adaptive detection and rollout guards (hysteresis + KV-aware thresholds)
author: Aisha Tanaka
description: Adds adaptive performance canary detection and rollout guard enhancements. Motivations: 1) reduce noisy false positives from baseline drift and KV cache warmup, 2) enable safe automated rollouts with hysteresis and multi-metric decisioning, 3) expose config for per-model sensitivity. Changes include a new detector that computes dynamic baselines using exponential windowing, KV-cache aware latency bucketing, hysteresis counters for both latency and throughput regressions, and a rollout controller integration that supports staged traffic shifts and automatic rollback on sustained regressions. Includes updated dashboards, new e2e perf scenarios, and documentation for tuning sensitivity per workload. This PR is targeted at the perf-canary service and rollout controller and has accompanying unit and integration tests. High level checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implementation - [x] KV-cache aware metrics + exporter changes - [x] Rollout guard integration + staged traffic operator - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf canary e2e scenarios added to perf-lab - [x] Docs and release notes

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice work. Two questions: 1) how does the detector behave for extremely low QPS models? 2) please add a unit test for the hysteresis counter when toggling across the threshold boundary.

Aisha Tanaka: Thanks Diego. For low QPS models the detector switches to a quantile-based baseline (see detector.py:line ~210) and increases the smoothing window; added test test_low_qps_quantile_baseline in tests/perf/test_adaptive_detector.py.
Maya Chen: The rollout integration looks good, but controller metrics emitted during rollback are missing trace ids which makes debugging harder. Can you add trace propagation to staged_operator.go?
Aisha Tanaka: Added trace propagation and unit test to ensure trace id flows through staged operator (controllers/rollout/staged_operator.go).
Connor Li: Can we make the default sensitivity conservative (reduce false positives)? Also please update docs with recommended defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted.
Aisha Tanaka: Updated defaults in canary_config.proto and added a Dedicated vs Hosted tuning section in docs/perf_canary/tuning.md.
release_notes: Improved performance canary detection: adaptive baselines, KV-cache aware latency bucketing, hysteresis-based rollout guards, staged traffic operator with automatic rollback. See docs/perf_canary/tuning.md for configuration and tuning guidance.
notes: Follow-up: monitor perf-canary->rollout latencies for first 48 hours post-merge and consider lowering sensitivity for models with <5 QPS. Rollout of config defaults will be phased via feature flag.
